Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Taylor Kim, CFO; Morgan Patel, COO; Riley Chen, CMO; Casey Wong, CTO; Jordan Reyes, CDO; and Alex Taylor, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, CEO of ShopSphere Inc.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust marketplace dynamics including the positive shifts in seller behavior following our recent fee structure refinements, alongside accelerated growth from targeted promotional campaigns that boosted traffic and conversions. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV, which hit new highs, alongside improvements in average order value and order frequency reflecting evolving customer habits toward more frequent, convenience-driven purchases.

Our focus remains on scaling international expansion, where we've made meaningful progress in Europe, APAC, and Latin America, with GMV contributions surging and active users expanding rapidly. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our next-generation AI personalization tools, which we believe will significantly enhance conversion rates and customer lifetime value across categories.

We are investing heavily in logistics network enhancements and supply chain resilience to counter ongoing disruptions from port congestion and carrier surcharges.

We are focused on improving operational efficiencies in fulfillment and last-mile delivery.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia.

We are enhancing our customer experience through advanced recommendation engines and loyalty programs.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability goals, including reductions in packaging waste.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our Q2 revenue was $3.05 billion, an increase of 18% year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.4%, driven by a favorable category mix shift toward higher-margin electronics and beauty, fulfillment efficiencies from new micro-centers, and take rate expansion from seller tier migrations. Operating expenses were $674 million, representing 22.1% of revenue. Marketing spend remained disciplined at $320 million, or 10.5% of revenue, reflecting optimized ROAS from AI-targeted campaigns.

Turning to the marketplace dynamics, specifically the impact of our recent fee structure updates implemented in Q1. As many of you know, we announced a refined tiered fee model for our ShopSphere Marketplace last quarter, aimed at balancing seller economics with platform investments in AI-driven personalization, logistics expansion, and fraud prevention. Let me break this down with the data we've seen so far—it's been transformative for seller behavior and positions us strongly against competitors like Amazon Seller Central and Walmart Marketplace.

First, a quick recap of the changes: We introduced three seller tiers—Starter for 0-10k GMV per month at 12% referral fee, Growth for 10k-100k GMV at 10% with waived listing fees, and Enterprise for 100k+ GMV at 8% with priority fulfillment slots and advanced analytics. We also adjusted fulfillment fees by 5-7% upward for standard shipping to fund our new ShopSphere Fulfillment Network hubs, while offering volume discounts up to 15% for high-density categories like apparel and consumer electronics. These were benchmarked against industry averages—Amazon's effective take rate around 15-20% post-FBA, and Shopify's merchant fees averaging 2.9% plus $0.30, but without our scale in traffic and logistics.

The results speak for themselves. Post-update, we've seen a 22% YoY increase in net new active sellers, reaching 1.2 million unique sellers globally by quarter-end—our highest quarterly ramp since the post-pandemic boom. Churn among existing sellers dropped to just 4.2% from 7.8% pre-update, as measured by our Seller NPS, which jumped 18 points to 72. Sellers are migrating aggressively to higher tiers: 65% of Starter-tier sellers upgraded within 60 days, driving a 14% lift in overall platform take rate to 11.8%. This mirrors trends in peer platforms; for instance, when eBay tweaked its final value fees in 2023, they saw similar tier migration but with higher churn due to less robust seller tools.

Listings activity exploded: Total SKUs grew 28% QoQ to 450 million, with a pronounced pivot to high-velocity categories. Fashion and beauty sellers, 32% of our GMV, increased listings by 35%, optimizing for our new dynamic pricing algorithms that recommend 10-20% AOV uplifts via AI bundle suggestions—like bundling Nike sneakers with complementary accessories for a 15% conversion boost. Electronics sellers shifted 18% more volume to premium SFN fulfillment, reducing delivery times to under 48 hours and lifting repeat purchase rates by 12%.

Regionally, North America at 65% of GMV saw US SMBs adopt tiers fastest at 72% migration rate, fueled by 25 new SFN hubs, countering Amazon's FBA fee hikes and pulling 45k cross-platform sellers via our one-click import tool. EMEA at 18% of GMV had slower uptake at 55% due to GDPR costs, but UK and German fashion merchants surged 40% in ad spend on our Marketplace Ads, with EU take rate at 12.5%. APAC at 17% exploded with 150k new sellers up 40% YoY embracing Enterprise tiers, though we addressed cross-border fee sensitivity with localization like JPY-denominated fees for Japan.

We've supercharged adaptation with Seller Hub 2.0: real-time fee simulators predicting 95% accurate net margins, API integrations for ERP like NetSuite, and ML-powered assortment optimizers flagging $2.5B in underperforming inventory. Early adopters saw 22% GMV growth per A/B tests.

Financially, marketplace revenue grew 31% YoY to $1.8B, services revenue up 42% to $720M—now 40% of total. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 250bps to 28%, as higher tiers and SFN utilization at 85% offset investments.

Our net income for the quarter was $128 million, or $0.58 per share. This was up 22% year-over-year on net income and 21% on EPS, significantly exceeding consensus expectations of $112 million net income and $0.50 EPS—a 14% and 16% beat, respectively. Fully diluted shares were 221 million, flat YoY after $75 million in repurchases. This beat stemmed from top-line momentum, with GMV at $12.4 billion up 24% YoY outpacing guided 21%, marketplace revenues up 28% on 15.2% take rates, and AOV up 8% to $85. Gross margins expanded 210bps ahead of guidance via logistics savings, op ex down to 22.1% with CAC at $18 and LTV/CAC at 17.8x. Prime memberships grew 31% to 45 million driving 55% of GMV.

On GMV specifically, we delivered $12.4 billion, up 24% YoY and 12% QoQ, beating our guidance high end. This outpaced industry 10-12% growth, with active buyers up 12% to 145 million on AI recs now at 42% of GMV. QoQ reflected back-to-school and bundles lifting orders per buyer to 4.2 and AOV to $112. North America grew 25% YoY, APAC 42%, EMEA 19%.

Promotional activities accounted for 35% of GMV, driving 28% YoY GMV growth to levels outpacing peers. They generated 45 million incremental visits, boosting traffic 32% and conversions to 4.2%. Bundling lifted AOV 7% to $85, with regional uplifts like 30% in NA, 45% in APAC. Margins compressed 180bps to 27.5% from discount depth, but AI optimization yielded 3x ROAS on $150M spend, NovaPerks offset with 25% growth to 12M members.

AOV trends at $52.30 marked 14% YoY and 5% QoQ growth, outpacing guidance. AI personalization at 78% of pages lifted upsells 22%, free shipping thresholds and OmniPrime perks added more, category shifts to electronics/home. Regionally, NA at $58.40 up 16%, Europe $48.20 up 11%.

We ended the quarter with $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of 20-25% revenue growth, $2.35-$2.45 EPS.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Patel to discuss operations.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on network expansion and resilience against supply chain disruptions. Our shipping times improved by 22%, with same-day in 85% of US orders under $50. Fulfillment costs improved 15% YoY to 12.5% of GMV. We are implementing RouteFlow AI across 85% of our 120 FCs.

On logistics and shipping costs, they hit 14.2% of revenue, up 160bps YoY due to carrier surcharges and disruptions. Total spend $285M up 22%, outbound $162M up 28% from 15-20% surcharges and port issues like Red Sea rerouting adding 10-14 days, spiking inbound freight 40%. NA saw 19% inbound rise, Europe 25% from Ukraine effects, APAC buffered but typhoon-hit. We mitigated with carrier diversification saving $18M, AI dynamic routing cutting 14% per package, nearshoring to Mexico, and last-mile with DoorDash trimming returns 8%. LaaS generates $45M ARR offsetting 16% costs. Q3 guidance 13.8-14.5%.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Chen.

Riley Chen:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from flash sales and personalized coupons, driving 35% of GMV, and loyalty campaigns boosting frequency. Customer acquisition costs were $18, down 11%. Our brand awareness increased by 22%. We are focusing on ROAS optimization and social commerce.

Order frequency rose 12% YoY to 5.1 orders per active customer, up 3% QoQ, outperforming peers. New cohorts at 2.8 orders up 25%, mature at 7.2 up 8%. Shifts to micro-moments fueled by Auto-Ship at 28% of orders, averaging 8.7 for subs. NA up 15% to 5.6 on same-day, Europe 9% to 4.7, APAC 14% to 4.9 on live-buy. AI nudges and gamification boost app frequency to 6.2.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Wong.

Casey Wong:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization like NovaRec and RouteFlow, and warehouse robotics. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in AR/VR try-on and headless commerce for faster launches.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Reyes.

Jordan Reyes:
Thanks, Casey. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 18% improvement in conversion rates because of AI rec engines and frequency boosters. We are also focusing on privacy with server-side tagging.

Now I'll turn it over to Alex Taylor.

Alex Taylor:
Thanks, Jordan. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 25% through recycled packaging at 45% internationally and optimized routing. We are committed to nearshoring incentives and Green Deal alignment.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, could you expand on the GMV growth details versus guidance and what drove the beat?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Sarah. As Taylor detailed, Q2 GMV of $12.4B was up 24% YoY and 12% QoQ, high end of our range. Active buyers up 12% on AI recs at 42% of GMV, bundles lifting AOV and orders per buyer. Regional strength in APAC 42% and NA 25%, validating our investments.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Patel:
Great, thanks. Taylor, on promotions—how did they impact profitability, and what's the outlook?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, promos drove 35% of GMV, 28% growth overall, with 45M visits and 4.2% conversions. Compressed margins 180bps but 3x ROAS via AI, Perks stabilizing EBITDA at 11.8%. Q4 personalized stacks for 15% AOV lift with less drag.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Morgan, thoughts on logistics costs and supply chain disruptions?

Morgan Patel:
Lisa, disruptions added 160bps to 14.2% of rev, with $285M spend from surcharges and Red Sea delays. Mitigated half via diversification, AI saving 14%, nearshoring. Q3 moderating to 13.8-14.5% as hubs ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Barclays.

David Wong:
Thanks. Riley, on order frequency changes and customer habits?

Riley Chen:
David, up 12% to 5.1, driven by subs at 28% of orders, 8.7 avg. Micro-moments post-COVID, regional surges like NA 5.6 on same-day. Tech like AI nudges for more.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Reyes with Citi.

Emma Reyes:
Hi, Casey—tech investments supporting AOV trends?

Casey Wong:
Emma, NovaRec at 78% pages lifted upsells 22%, AR/VR 15% conversions, free shipping nudges. Category shifts and bundles key to $52.30 AOV up 14%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Taylor with RBC.

Tom Taylor:
Thanks. Jordan R., data initiatives on international?

Jordan Reyes:
Tom, AI personalization yielding 18% CTR in APAC, LTV $420 intl up 65%. Inventory pooling cut stockouts 34%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Nina Gupta with Deutsche Bank.

Nina Gupta:
Alex, international expansion metrics?

Alex Taylor:
Nina, intl GMV $2.8B up 48% YoY, 28% total, revenue +52%. Europe 61%, APAC 72%, LatAm 39%. MAUs 45M up 35%, CAC $18 down 22%, EBITDA 14.2%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
